_comment: EXTERNAL ground truth, hand-checked against the live game / published stats.
This file is the real accuracy gate: it is NOT generated from the game files,
so it independently pins the ingestion chain (milli-tile units, the shared
power ladder, the rarity offset, truncation, projectile damage lookup).
Add an entry only when you have actually confirmed the number. Never
regenerate this file from a build -- that would make the gate circular.
'display_level' is the rarity-independent level the game shows (11 = tournament standard).

Knight._source: confirmed: 1,766 HP, 202 damage per hit, 168 DPS, 1.2s hit speed, 3 elixir Common

Pekka._source: 3760 HP confirmed live; damage 842 established by interaction breakpoints (see tests/test_interactions.py)

ArcherQueen._source: champion rarity offset check: base 391 at power index 0 x2.56 = 1000 at display 11

Rocket._source: well-established tournament-standard value; pins the spell projectile-damage path

Arrows._source: 122 is PER WAVE; 3 waves of 10 projectiles 200ms apart, so 366 against a target that stays put

Fireball._source: tournament-standard damage, 2.5-tile radius, reduced crown-tower damage

Zap._source: tournament-standard 192 damage; pins the area-effect damage path

Lightning._source: tournament-standard 1057; pins the area-effect -> projectile chain

Poison._source: tournament-standard 92 damage/second over 8s; pins the buff DoT path

IceWizard._source: tournament-standard 688 HP / 89 damage; pins the same-name character fallback

ThreeMusketeers._source: reworked card; 3 units from an explicit SummonCharactersList

engine_constants._comment: Structural facts read out of the game files and cross-checked against live play.
engine_constants._geometry_source: tilemaps/tilemap.csv from the APK, 36x64 half-tile bitfield; 141 of 158 arena rows use it
engine_constants._footprint_source: BLOCKED region in tilemap.csv at cells x15-20,y3-8; PrincessTower has no blocked footprint and uses CollisionRadius=1000 (1 tile)

open_questions.question: P.E.K.K.A damage at display level 11: extracted data gives 842; some public stat sites report 510.
open_questions.resolution: 842 is correct. A same-level Musketeer has 721 HP, and P.E.K.K.A one-shotting a Musketeer is a well-established interaction that 510 cannot produce. The breakpoint also cuts the other way correctly: 842 does NOT one-shot a 1766 HP Knight, which matches play. The public 510 figure is stale. Locked in by tests/test_interactions.py.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: (kept for provenance) read Damage on the in-game card page.

open_questions.question: Arrows deals 122 per projectile across 3 waves of 10. How many waves actually land on one stationary unit, and does the in-game 'Damage' figure show per-wave or total?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether Arrows clears 230 HP Minions, which is its defining use. Affects any spell with ProjectileWaves or MultipleProjectiles (Arrows, Hunter, Princess).
open_questions.how_to_resolve: M5 models waves explicitly; then assert Arrows clears a Minion Horde and Hunter's point-blank burst kills what it should. Until then do not treat `damage` on these three as a single hit.
open_questions.resolution: Per wave. Arrows fires 3 waves of 10 projectiles 200ms apart, and the 122 figure is one projectile, so a target that stays in the area takes 3 x 122 = 366. Confirmed by the card's canonical kills: 366 clears Minions and Minion Horde (230), Goblins (202), Spear Goblins (133) and Princess (261), while a single wave would only clear Skeletons and Bats (81) - which is plainly not what Arrows does. The wave structure is also why observed damage looks inconsistent: a unit that leaves the area, or dies to an early wave, takes fewer than three.
open_questions.still_to_implement: Waves are not simulated yet - Arrows is a spell and spells land in M5. Hunter's 10 pellets and Princess' 5 are a different mechanic (one shot, spread by distance) and remain unresolved.

open_questions.question: Do Crown Towers scale on the card PowerLevelMultiplier ladder, or on their own per-level percentage?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Tower hitpoints set every damage race in the game. cr-sim currently applies the card ladder, giving Princess 3584 / King 6144 at level 11, which is very likely too high.
open_questions.evidence: globals.csv carries a separate tower progression the cards do not use: HITPOINT_INCREASE_PERCENT_PER_TOWER_LEVEL=8, HITPOINT_INCREASE_PERCENT_PER_KING_LEVEL=7, *_AFTER_TOURNAMENTCAP=10, *_AT_TOURNAMENTCAP=10, TOWER_SCALING_START_EXP_LEVEL=9. A flat +8%/level on the level-1 base gives Princess 2520 at level 11 instead of 3584.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Read Princess and King Tower hitpoints off the in-game tower card at a known King level, then fit which of the candidate formulas reproduces it. Must be settled in M2, when towers start fighting.
open_questions.resolution: Towers are NOT on the card ladder. They accumulate a flat percentage of their level-1 base: 8%/level for a Princess Tower, 7% for the King, switching to 10%/level past TOWER_SCALING_START_EXP_LEVEL=9. Two independent supports: the globals themselves, and published descriptions of tower progression stating '+8% per level from 1 to 9, +10% from 9 to 13'. A third check falls out for free - published tower hitpoints are all divisible by 14, which this formula reproduces automatically for every level (1400 x integer%/100), and the card ladder does not. Level 11: Princess 2576, King 4224. The card ladder gave 3584, a 39% error.

open_questions.question: Are the bridges 2 or 3 tiles wide?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Bridge width sets how many units can cross abreast and how spells cover a crossing push.
open_questions.evidence: Every non-event tilemap in build 150535029 has 2-tile bridges (cells x5-8 and x27-30 across all four river rows), and 141 of 158 arena rows point at that one tilemap. Public descriptions say 2 tiles in Arenas 1-6 and 8-9 but 3 tiles in Arenas 7 and 10-23, which this build's data does not reproduce anywhere.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Likely the public figure describes the visual bridge art, or predates a geometry unification. If a future APK extraction shows a 3-tile tilemap, tests/test_arena_and_battle.py::test_bridges_are_two_tiles_wide_in_this_build will fail and flag it.

open_questions.question: Do buildings collide as squares or as circles?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether a unit can clip a building's corner, and how tightly troops pack around a Cannon or Tombstone. Affects every surround and every building-block placement.
open_questions.evidence: The King Tower's blocked footprint in tilemap.csv is a clean 3.0x3.0 tile SQUARE (cells x15-20, y3-8), not a disc, and buildings are placed on tile centres. But the only per-entity extent in the data is CollisionRadius, a single scalar (KingTower 1400, PrincessTower 1000), which is circular by nature. PrincessTower has no blocked footprint at all. cr-sim's fixed.circles_overlap currently treats everything as a circle.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: M3 (collision). Test by walking a troop diagonally at a Cannon's corner and comparing where it stops against the real game.

open_questions.question: Sparky (ZapMachine) sets LoadFirstHit=true, which cr-sim does not implement.
open_questions.why_it_matters: For every other unit LoadTime is a one-time windup before the first hit. LoadFirstHit makes the unit pay that charge before EVERY shot, and three globals govern it: LOGIC_LOAD_FIRST_HIT_RESET_TIMER_AFTER_ATTACK, ..._RESET_TIMER_WHEN_ZAPPED and ..._KEEP_LOADED_AFTER_DISCARD (all true). The middle one is the famous 'a stun resets Sparky's charge' interaction, which is most of how the card is countered.
open_questions.evidence: Exactly one entity in the build sets it: ZapMachine, LoadTime=3000, HitSpeed=4000. Because HitSpeed exceeds LoadTime the firing rhythm happens to look similar without it - what is missing is the reset-on-stun, not the cadence. LoadAfterRetarget is a schema column no entity uses.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Implement alongside stun buffs: a LoadFirstHit unit re-pays LoadTime before each shot, keeps its progress when it loses a target, and loses all of it when stunned.

open_questions.question: Lightning fires 4 bolts in cr-sim where the real card fires 3.
open_questions.why_it_matters: A fourth bolt is a third more damage from a 6-elixir spell, and changes which pushes it answers.
open_questions.evidence: AEO.Lightning has LifeDuration=1500 and HitSpeed=460. With the first application landing immediately (which Poison requires - it produces exactly the documented 736 damage, and delaying it gives 7 ticks instead of 8) that window fits applications at 0, 460, 920 and 1380 = four. Delaying the first application gives three but breaks Poison. So the two spells disagree about the first-application rule under any single interpretation.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Either the engine caps bolts by a count not present in this data, or the AEO lifetime is measured differently from how cr-sim reads it. Count the bolts and time the cloud in-game. Note Lightning has no OneHitPerTarget flag, so distinct-target selection is also inferred from the card's known behaviour rather than stated.
open_questions.resolution: An area effect fires LifeDuration // HitSpeed times, not however many a timer started on contact happens to fit. Lightning is 1500ms over a 460ms interval: the timer model fits four bolts into that window, the division gives three, and three is what the card fires. The reading costs nothing anywhere else -- Poison (32), Tornado (21), Earthquake (30) and every one-shot effect come out identical under both models, so Lightning is the only case in the build that distinguishes them. Poison's verified 736 is unaffected because its damage comes from the buff it applies, not from the cloud's own application count.

open_questions.question: AttractPercentage (Tornado 360) is named like a percentage. Is it a percentage of the pulled unit's own speed, or a flat rate in tiles/minute like every other speed in this data?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether Tornado drags a Golem as fast as a Hog Rider, and whether it can pull a unit from its edge to its centre within its 1050ms lifetime at all -- which is the entire card.
open_questions.resolution: A flat rate in tiles per minute. Tornado's radius is 5.5 tiles and its LifeDuration is 1050ms; at 360 tiles/min (6 tiles/s) an edge unit reaches the centre in 917ms, just inside its lifetime, which is exactly how the card behaves. Read as a percentage of the unit's own speed it would take a 45-speed Golem 2037ms -- twice the tornado's life, so a Golem would barely move -- and it would mean Tornado pulls fast units harder than slow ones, the opposite of a card that drags an entire push uniformly. The three other tornado buffs corroborate the scale: the Valkyrie and Wizard hero mini-tornadoes read 300 and 250 against smaller radii, and Super Archer's 450 x PushSpeedFactor 120. Implemented as its own tick phase (pull_units) so it moves units that are attacking, frozen, or otherwise not moving under their own power.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: (kept for provenance) time a Tornado dragging a Golem vs a Hog Rider the same distance; equal times confirm a flat rate.

open_questions.question: Heal Spirit's total healing at display level 11. The engine derives 400 (four applications of 100, 250ms apart over a 1000ms buff).
open_questions.why_it_matters: Heal is a 1-elixir card whose whole value is the size of the top-up; the mechanism is verified but the magnitude is not.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Damage a Knight in-game, drop a Heal Spirit on it, read the hitpoints back. The per-application rhythm (4 x 250ms) is already confirmed from HealPerSecond/HitFrequency/BuffTime and is not in question -- only the scaled total.

open_questions.question: A Clone's hitpoints. Every other detail of the spell is in the build -- the 0.25 tile offset (CLONE_DISTANCE_Y), that the shield is preserved (CLONE_PRESERVE_SHIELD), that a clone cannot be cloned (CLONE_CLONED_UNITS) -- but the clone's own hitpoint value is in none of them.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the whole balance of the card: full damage on a body that dies to anything. Getting it wrong in either direction turns a 3-elixir damage multiplier into either a no-op or a second push.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Clone a Knight in-game and hit the clone once with anything. The engine uses 1, which is the card's universally documented behaviour, but it is applied as known behaviour rather than read from the files and should be confirmed.
open_questions.note: Searched ACTION.CloneAction, BUFF.Clone and every CLONE_* global in this build; none carries a hitpoint value. Likely hardcoded client-side.
